text:
maria (sales): Quick sync — Simon from MeridianBank is asking if we can support a split-key BYOK flow for their PII pipeline. They want key material split across two HSMs, monthly rotation, and a strict 2-hour maintenance window for any key ceremony. Can we map this to Redwood’s options?
ajay (solutions): Short answer: yes, with caveats. We don't do built-in Shamir splitting inside the runtime. Typical patterns: 1) customer-side split/threshold (they hold parts, we accept a wrapped KEK), or 2) envelope with two KMS KEKs where both must XOR/unwrap client-side before we use — requires customer orchestration.
ajay (solutions): Important: if both HSMs must participate on every decryption, latency and availability are driven by the slowest KMS call. If they accept a single unwrapped KEK held by Redwood (customer-managed via HSM proxy), we can meet sub-15ms additional overhead on average.
tori (crypto-ops): To clarify: Meridian requires HSM attestation and FIPS 140-2/3 proof. We support CloudHSM/CloudKMS integrations and customer-managed HSM via our key-proxy. Attestation artifacts can be surfaced but the split-key ceremony itself would be customer-owned.
micah (eng): Ops notes — if customer opts for forced on-each-request unwrap (no caching), our runtime can call the KMS per-request but that will increase per-call cost and p95 latency by roughly 40-120ms depending on region/KMS. We can offer short-lived prefix caching of the derived DEK (configurable TTL) if the customer allows it in the contract.
simon (customer): @maria @ajay Clarify please — is there an option where you hold nothing but still run inference? We need zero-knowledge on raw KEK material.
ajay (solutions): Yes. Option A: Redwood holds only the wrapped DEK. The customer performs unwrap in their KMS and passes a short-lived envelope token to Redwood (customer-run unwrap). That requires a lightweight proxy or token exchange during POC. Option B: customer gives Redwood a CMK hosted in their HSM via our key-proxy but with strict access logging + attestation — Redwood never exports key material.
tori (crypto-ops): For compliance: we'll capture detailed audit logs (key usage, caller identity, request context) and provide them as part of the Private deployment package. Rotation: we can support automated rotation triggers, but the rotation process needs to be co-ordinated if customer executes a multi-custodian ceremony.
claire (legal): Note on rotation windows — if Meridian enforces a 2-hour blackout for production cutover, we need the SOW to state roll-back criteria and who’s responsible for the key ceremony. Any manual step from the customer side costs additional ops hours in the SOW.
maria (sales): Pricing implications: per-KMS-call cost + Redwood request overhead. For per-decrypt unwraps, estimate ~ $0.03-$0.08 per API call in added KMS fees depending on cloud vendor, plus our per-token/embedding charges. We'll put exact numbers in the quote.
simon (customer): We're cost-sensitive. Can you provide a sample SOW and a testing plan? We want clear success criteria before committing to Dedicated.
ajay (solutions): Will do. Quick POC proposal (high level): 1) 2-week sandbox with staging HSMs, 2) sample workload (~100 TPS peak) with both unwrap-on-each-request and cached-DEK modes, 3) run perf tests p50/p95 latency, KMS-call counts, error + fallback behavior, 4) deliver attestation artifacts and runbook. Success = ability to sustain 80 TPS with <200ms p95 and no lost keys during a planned rotation.
micah (eng): I'll add a short config snippet we can run in staging for the cached mode: 
```
redwood.deploy: 
  key_management: 
    mode: envelope_cache 
    dek_cache_ttl_ms: 30000 
    kms_backends: ["proj-cloudhsm-a", "proj-cloudhsm-b"]
```
(We also include optional unwrap_on_request: true for the strict mode.)
ajay (solutions): We'll attach a pricing appendix showing incremental costs for unwrap-on-each-request, plus estimated ops hours for multi-custodian ceremony (we typically budget 12-24 engineering hours for runbook & dry-run).
simon (customer): One more: we need the ability to rotate without rolling keys for previously issued tokens (backwards compatibility). Can Redwood support DEK versioning so older tokens still decrypt?
tori (crypto-ops): Yes — we support DEK versioning and can keep historical keys in a locked state for a configurable retention period. We can also enforce key expiry at token-level in the POC to test compatibility.
claire (legal): Also add in the DPA note about escrow — if they want key escrow, define who can request key release and under what legal process. That belongs in the contract.
maria (sales): Action items: @ajay to draft the POC SOW and runbook by EOD tomorrow, @micah to prepare the staging config + perf test harness, @tori to list required attestation artifacts, @claire to draft contract language options for escrow and rotation window. Simon — we'll loop you in for a kickoff once SOW is ready. :thumbsup:
ajay (solutions): Ack — starting SOW draft now.
simon (customer): Thanks team, appreciate the speed. We'll review SOW and aim for a kickoff next week.
